overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the nonunion personnel from the executive session notice and by not recording the date and time of the same-day amended notices, but found no violation on the other alleged notice defects.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the posted notice for the December 20, 2023 meeting was actually a notice for an Everett Retirement Board meeting.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Committee complied with the Open Meeting Law’s notice posting requirements.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice failed to name the two Superintendent finalists the Committee planned to interview.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, because the Committee made efforts to seek guidance and promptly amended the notice to include the names of both candidates after speaking with an Assistant Attorney General, we decline to find a violation of the Open Meeting Law in this case.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session topic omitted the specific nonunion personnel with whom the Committee would negotiate.
allegations.key_passage: We, therefore, find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to identify on the December 20, 2023, meeting notice the nonunion personnel.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice did not record the date and time it was amended on the day of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find here that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to conspicuously record thereon or therewith the date and time that the revised notices were posted.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
